newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices firm as supply thins.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices firm as supply thins.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices rose around one-quarter of a point in early afternoon trade on Thursday, bolstered by stronger U.S. Treasuries and views that there were fewer supplies of attractive new municipal issues.
Competitive sales slated for Thursday add up to approximately $373 million in 26 offerings, down from the unusually high volumes seen in mid-October.
The largest competitive issue was Virginia Transportation Board's sale of $184 million, which were won by Lehman at a true interest cost of 5.34 percent.

"The Virginia Transportation (issue) looked a little high, but Virginia is a state that usually trades higher. And since there are no bonds around, people who are looking for block size will probably go for these because there's nothing else around," a trader said.

While complaints that some of the new issues have been agressively priced have been heard over the past few weeks, traders said that the market remains in a fairly bullish mode, with players focusing on favourable features that they can get with new debt.
"We have a lot of people looking for new stuff, good calls, good structure," a trader said.
Other traders suggested that the Street was not the major buyer, as dealers appeared to be finding accounts for new issues, removing pressure on prices.

Among the eight negitiated offerings that total $411 million, Chicago Toll Bridge led the list with a sale of $183 million of Skyway bonds, which were priced at a top yield of 5.799 percent in 2023, according to PaineWebber.

The firmer tone in the U.S. Treasury market, which was encouraged by the latest economic data that suggests the economy still is growing fairly slowly, also helped pull up the prices of municipal bonds.
The Consumper Price Index, the key indicator released, rose 0.3 percent overall, and gained 0.2 percent, when the more volatile food and energy prices are excluded.
These results matched the forecasts seen in a Reuters consensus survey of economists.
December Treasury bond futures rose 14 ticks to 115-5/32, while December municipal bond futures, which recently have lagged, also gained 14 ticks to 117-9/32.
The MOB spread stood at 68 ticks, little changed.

Actively quoted issues in the secondary market included Alabama Water Pollution Control Authority Revolving Fund of August 2020, which pay a 5-1/2 percent coupon, and were bid at 5.69 percent, down two basis points from levels seen on Wednesday.
And Ohio State Turnpike Community Revenues of February 2026, which carry a 5-1/2 percent coupon, were bid at 5.65 percent, down two basis points.
